- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are trending upward, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to align with momentum.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated overshoot; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or 1.5x prior high.
- Model underestimates in low-sentiment, stable-price environments; add 5–15% buffer if sentiment is flat or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 5–7 days show strong trend, apply decay factor (e.g., 0.8–0.9) to forecast to avoid over-leverage.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match sentiment cycle phase (e.g., if sentiment rising, forecast should rise faster than model).
